objectives.text: Win the Mbanié, Cocotiers and Conga islands dispute with Gabon in law. The case went to the ICJ under a 2016 Special Agreement after UN mediation (proceedings instituted 5 March 2021); the merits judgment of 19 May 2025 went largely in Equatorial Guinea's favour, holding that the 1974 Bata Convention was not a treaty with the force of law between the parties and that the title which counts is the one Spain held on 12 October 1968, which Equatorial Guinea succeeded to. Reported vote 13-2 (search summary, not verified).

grand_strategy.reading: On the sources read here, Equatorial Guinea runs two tracks: it takes its border dispute with Gabon to court when the law can be made to favour it, and it enforces control at sea with the means it has, which has since become a tribunal suit. The card is thin because the sources read here do not cover the Obiang succession, China's port and debt, the United States, France, Spain, Cameroon, CEMAC or the decline of oil and gas; those gaps are logged in JOURNAL, not filled from memory. Until they are sourced, read this card as the island and sea file only.

stances.note: Our reading (C): the grade rests on the open sovereignty dispute over Mbanié, Cocotiers and Conga, taken to the ICJ under a 2016 Special Agreement and decided on 19 May 2025 largely in Equatorial Guinea's favour. Bond grievance: the 1972 expulsion of Equatorial Guinean soldiers from Mbanié, which Gabon has held since (search summary of press coverage, not opened). Rival rather than adversary: the sources describe a legal dispute with no declared aim of Gabon's disappearance. Trend stable: a 2026 headline reports both sides applying the judgment, read as a headline only and not verified, so no trend is claimed beyond stable.

stances_toward.note: Rival, not adversary, from Libreville's side. The ICJ ruling of 19 May 2025 gave Mbanie, Cocotiers and Conga largely to Equatorial Guinea, and the open wound is the 1972 expulsion of Equatorial Guinean soldiers from Mbanie (press summary, not opened). The sources describe a legal sovereignty dispute with no declared aim to end the Equatoguinean state, so rival; the grievance is the bond. Trend stable: no post-judgment escalation or thaw is reported, and the 2026 headline on implementation is not verified. Our reading (C); the press reports the ruling, not Libreville's own statements.

stances_toward.note: Rival, cooling, from Majuro's side. The flag state calls the 2022 boarding and seizure of the Heroic Idun, and the nine-month detention of its crew, illegal; in October 2025 it sued Equatorial Guinea at ITLOS for nearly US$60 million, the latest move in the relation. Two states with competing interests in the same waters, and no source has the Marshall Islands seeking the end of Equatorial Guinea, so rival and not adversary. Bond none: no kinship or open historical grievance is found. Our reading (C); the sources are press reports of the case.
